Show a folder as an interactive map

Source: R/map_folder.R
map_folder.Rd

Scans path and opens it as a network graph in the browser. A big project folder with many levels is hard to take in through the file explorer: you see one level at a time and have nowhere to write down what matters. The map shows the whole structure at once, sized by bytes or number of files, and lets you add what you know: tags (Core, Important, Unclear, Outdated), notes, and your own relations between folders and files, such as "input to" or "depends on".

Usage

map_folder(
  path = ".",
  ignore = folder_ignore(),
  notes = file.path(path, ".foldermap.json"),
  show_files = TRUE,
  server = requireNamespace("httpuv", quietly = TRUE),
  open = interactive(),
  file = NULL,
  gitignore = FALSE,
  detect = TRUE
)

Arguments

path

The folder to show.

ignore

Names to skip, see folder_ignore().

notes

The file holding tags, notes and relations. Defaults to .foldermap.json inside the folder, so it follows the project.

show_files

Show the files from the start, not just the folders? Can be switched in the map too. At most 40 files per folder are drawn at a time; the rest are gathered in one node you can click.

server

Start a local server that saves the notes to notes? Needs httpuv.

open

Open the map in the browser?

file

Without a server only: where the HTML file is written. Defaults to a temporary file.

gitignore

Also skip what git ignores? See scan_folder().

detect

Read the scripts in the folder and suggest relations from the paths they use? See the section on suggestions.

Value

Invisibly, the address (with a server) or the path to the HTML file.

Details

Double-click a folder to unfold it. Select a node to see its size, file types, and largest and most recently changed files, and to give it a tag, a note or a relation to another node.

Relations the map suggests

Drawing every relation by hand is the slow part, so the map proposes some. With detect = TRUE the R, R Markdown and Quarto scripts in the folder are read for quoted paths that point at something else in the folder, and the call around the path decides the label: a file handed to read_csv() or readRDS() is "input to" the script, one handed to write_csv() or ggsave() is one the script "writes", and a source()d file is "sourced by" it. Files with the same name and size are proposed as "copy of" each other.

These are suggestions only. They are drawn dotted, listed in the panel, and become relations when you add them; a dismissed suggestion is remembered in the notes file and not proposed again. The scripts are read as text, never run, so a path built at run time (paste0(dir, name)) is not found. file.path() and here() calls made of plain strings are.

Where the notes are kept

In .foldermap.json inside the scanned folder. That is deliberate, rather than the browser's own storage: the file follows the project, can be shared with colleagues and put under version control. It only changes when you change a tag, a note or a relation. What is unfolded, the layout and where the nodes sit is personal and changes with every click, so that is remembered per folder in your own cache (tools::R_user_dir("pathr", "cache")) instead.

Writing the file takes a small local server, which needs httpuv. It listens on 127.0.0.1, reachable only from your own machine, and every request must carry a random token, so other web pages in your browser cannot read the folder or overwrite the notes. The server also lets the ↻ button rescan the folder and the "Open" and "Show in explorer" buttons reach the file on disk. It runs until the R session ends or stop_folder_map() is called.

Without httpuv (server = FALSE) a single self-contained HTML file is written. Existing notes are shown, but new ones are kept in the browser only; use "Export" and save the file as .foldermap.json in the folder.

Does anything go online?

No. The scan happens in R, the page is served from your own machine, and the graph's JavaScript library (vis-network) ships with the package. Nothing is fetched from outside and nothing is sent anywhere.

See also

folder_notes() reads the notes back into R and folder_guide() writes them up; scan_folder() gives the file listing the map is built from.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
map_folder("C:/projects/big-project")

# without a server, as a file you can pass on
map_folder(".", server = FALSE, file = "folder-map.html")
} # }
